## Changes since `v0.7.1`

### Features

- read the known_hosts files ~/.ssh/config names with UserKnownHostsFile and GlobalKnownHostsFile when a host's key is checked, for the host and for the saved connection's name, with their tokens filled in, where only the default files were read, so a company file of host keys or @cert-authority lines that ssh is told about counts in tTerm too; they are read besides the default files rather than instead of them, which trusts nothing the user's own files do not list, and the import no longer calls UserKnownHostsFile unsupported ([4c0873a0](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/4c0873a05040b808451dae8a1d488b3b9cb732d3))
- fill in the rest of the % tokens ssh allows in IdentityFile and CertificateFile: %l and %L with the name of this machine, %j with the last jump host of ProxyJump, %k with the host name as typed, %i with the user id on Linux and macOS, and %C with the connection hash ssh makes of %l%h%p%r%j, so a key stored as ~/.ssh/keys/%C is found instead of passed over with a warning ([cd3fb6cd](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/cd3fb6cd1024c920951b2b60541113809394d28f))
- check host keys against OpenSSH's known_hosts files before tTerm's own record, so a host ssh already trusts is not asked about again and a host that proves itself with a host certificate can be reached: a key listed for the host is trusted, a key marked @revoked is refused, a different key of the same type listed for it is shown as a changed key, and a host with an @cert-authority trusted for it is asked for a certificate, which is accepted when that authority signed it for the host as ssh checks it (a host certificate within its validity, naming the host among its principals or naming none, without critical options) and refused otherwise; hashed host names and \[host\]:port entries are matched, and the files are read on every connection as ssh reads them ([ad9a0bfb](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/ad9a0bfb7d83d354dbe30c245fa5f416ac2fe694))
- read ~/.ssh/config includes the way ssh does: a relative Include path is looked up in ~/.ssh from every file, where it was looked up beside the file holding it, so an include nested in config.d/ found nothing; an Include under a Host or Match line now applies only where that line does, and the lines after it belong to the block above it again, where the included file's last Host line took them over; warnings about an included file now name that file and its line instead of a line number counted through every file ([64304ea7](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/64304ea75e8381b7420ea89e066c238ed4420fd4))
- fill in a host typed into the new tab launcher from what ~/.ssh/config sets for it even when the config does not list it by that name, since ssh applies wildcard and Match blocks to any name it is given but the launcher only knew the names on Host lines, so typing db9.corp.example.com under a Host *.corp.example.com that sets User and ProxyJump asked for a user and went straight to the host; resolve_ssh_config_host now reads the config for a typed name, and the launcher asks it a moment after typing pauses and uses the answer for the typed connection and the connection dialog it opens, without listing the host among the config's own ([c3fce2ea](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/c3fce2eaec60bc04c1306a1d7d153d1604ede2c4))
- fill in the % tokens and ${VAR} references of IdentityFile and CertificateFile in ~/.ssh/config, since a wildcard block now reaches every host it matches and a path like ~/.ssh/%h.key was saved as written, a key file that does not exist; %d, %h, %n, %p, %r, %u and %% are filled in for the host and each jump host, with the local user for %r when the config names no user as ssh does, and a path with a token tTerm cannot fill, such as %C, is passed over with a warning for the next one ([877fde25](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/877fde25b6af3762fc43fa426a2a5e311af8d238))
- read each jump host in ~/.ssh/config through its own Host block, as ssh does: ProxyJump bastion was saved as the literal host bastion on port 22 with the target's key, so a jump host known only by its alias could not be reached; a jump host now takes HostName, Port, User and IdentityFile from the blocks that match its name, with the user and port written in ProxyJump coming first and the target's key used only when it has none, the first jump host's own ProxyJump comes before it in the chain while later ones keep theirs out as ssh's -J does, and a jump host that leads back to one already on the way is skipped with a warning instead of looping ([476a8e06](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/476a8e067bd0091f6098cf15a6f5f4200d6187a0))
- apply Match blocks in ~/.ssh/config when importing, since they were skipped with a warning and the User, IdentityFile or ProxyJump they set for a group of hosts was lost: a Match block now applies when all its criteria hold for what the lines above it have set, as in ssh: host compares the HostName so far, originalhost the name as typed, user the User so far or the local user, localuser the local user, sessiontype a shell, and all always holds; Match final and canonical read the blocks a second time, matching Host lines against the HostName; exec, localnetwork, tagged, command and version cannot be checked during an import, and exec would run a command whenever the launcher lists the config, so those blocks are left out with a warning naming the line ([2fd12728](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/2fd1272848c9b625cd857100eb0c72099d9f31eb))
- apply wildcard Host blocks in ~/.ssh/config to the hosts they match, the way ssh reads its config: a block like Host *.corp.example.com that sets User, ProxyJump or IdentityFile was skipped on import, so its hosts came in without them and could not connect; every host now gets each option from the first block that sets it in file order, so options above the first Host and an early Host * win as they do in ssh, !patterns rule a block out, names match without case, HostName fills in %h, key files, certificates and forwards gather from every block with the host's own first, ProxyJump and ProxyCommand stop each other in the order they come, a repeated Host name is one entry, and a jump host's user comes from its own Host block ([72c36c0b](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/72c36c0b61ba2fe155ec1f6d20c27c1bbd64ec01))
- offer "Open as root with sudo" beside a "Permission denied" in the SFTP drawer: the drawer, working as the user, then switches to root and opens as root the folder the user was refused, which is not the one in view, since the drawer stays where it was when a folder cannot be opened; the loader keeps that folder for it; the drawer's error moves into SftpErrorAlert, which keeps index.tsx clear of its 500-line limit ([2223ee32](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/2223ee32a9265ed54790e86155c59455aa53322f))
- add a sudo switch to the SFTP drawer, beside its name, that makes the drawer work on the host as root: switched on it reads "root" in the destructive color and the header carries a red line along its top, every request of the drawer asks the backend for root, and the folder in view loads again as root; a switch sudo refuses or the user cancels goes back to working as the user and keeps the error in view; switched off, a folder only root could read gives way to the drawer's first folder; the switch starts off whenever the tab opens; a file opened from a drawer in sudo mode is read and saved as root, says "root" beside its name in the editor, and gets a tab apart from the same file opened as the user ([3a58bef7](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/3a58bef7e8dd2f0cae15b958d525a04b9da39bba))
- ask for the sudo password when the file manager opens a host as root and none is saved: the tab's sign-in dialog asks with the title "sudo password", and again, saying sudo turned the last one down, up to three times as sudo itself does; a saved password sudo refuses is followed by the question too, and a connection with sudo prompt filling turned off is always asked; the password stays in memory with the connection until it closes; only sudo's own steps are bounded by the channel timeout now, so a user taking their time to type is not cut off ([c105637f](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/c105637f14148c5acc140b95c2c4dc4cfaea83a1))
- let an SFTP connection work on the host as root through sudo, asked for with sftpSudo on the connection: such a connection pools apart from the user's, finds out once with sudo -k -n true whether the account needs a password, checks the saved sudo or login password with sudo -v on a channel whose input then ends so a wrong one fails at once, and starts every channel, the control session, the transfer lanes and the scripts for archives, search and command delete, as sudo -k with the password as the first line of its input, sending nothing on until the command run as root prints a ready line, so the password never reaches sftp-server and sudo's messages never reach the protocol; sftp-server is found where sshd_config names it, then where distributions install it; refusals are told apart by the step they happen at, since sudo 1.9 and sudo-rs word them differently, and keep sudo's own words; a folder seen as root is not saved as the last one; the tests in sudo/host_tests.rs run the handshake against scripts/sudo-test-host, whose accounts cover a password, NOPASSWD with fish, sudo for systemctl only, no sudo, and requiretty, and pass with sudo 1.9.15 and sudo-rs 0.2.13 ([237b619c](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/237b619c8798166197dd341d777b203bf3678928))
- have the crab knock in the SSH sign-in prompt and when a host's key is new: the connection waits at the door for the user's answer, so the crab takes the key icon's place beside the prompt's title and stands beside the unknown host key's title, knocking afresh for each host when tunnels queue several; a host whose key changed gets no crab, since a changed key may be an attack and the warning should not look playful ([de3fcb89](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/de3fcb891fac99b2381c65460d3a83e8993ac6f3))
- offer the crab as a style of the AI agent badge on a tab: "Crab pinching" while the agent works and "Crab knocking" while it waits for the user, in Settings > Appearance next to the other styles; the badge draws the small crab 18 px tall, the smallest at which its eyes and claws still read at 100% scaling, and the knock plays three times like the ripple of the other waiting marks, since an agent may wait for hours; picked for working, the crab becomes every loading spinner too, as the other working styles do; it keeps its own colors, so the settings say so instead of offering a color; a Crab component builds the layers from src/assets/crab and picks the small drawing below 32 px ([8ed4a284](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/8ed4a284f96180989516994ab9270006bdfe8891))
- show the crab pinching its claws on the splash screen while tTerm loads: the front-facing crab, a terminal window for a body with two eyes on top and a claw at each side, is drawn in scripts/app-icon/crab.mjs and written by pnpm icons:update to src/assets/crab as one SVG per moving part (the jaws, the arm, the eyes, the impact marks), plus a small version on an 18 px grid for badges; crab.css stacks the parts and animates each as its own HTML box rather than inside the SVG, since Chromium runs both on the compositor but WebKit, the webview on macOS and Linux, is only sure to do so for HTML boxes, and it already holds the knock that later asks for the user's attention; the splash drops the pulsing mascot.png, which stays for the README ([750d1a95](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/750d1a95c878eb2b9ad8caeed494571286919f64))
- search the saved connections a jump host logs in as: a hop's Connect as list was a plain select of every saved connection, hard to scan once there are many; it now opens a searchable list that finds a connection by its name, group, host or user, grouped as before, and a hop whose saved connection was deleted still says so on the button ([96b70f52](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/96b70f52cef9e67f73ad1360447d21083575c6ce))
- start local shells on macOS with shell integration by default: local bash, zsh and fish on macOS marked their commands only once the switch was turned on, so finished-command notifications and jumping between commands needed a trip to Settings first; the switch is now on by default on macOS and stays off on Linux, so it no longer travels with sync and moves to a new key, as every saved config holds the old one as off; an older config or backup that turned it on keeps it on, and one that left it off gets this device's default ([67d5e6eb](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/67d5e6eb09f4527cc6db7e49475cb70a183c5f10))
- start SSH sessions with shell integration by default: a connection had it only when its checkbox was ticked, so most never marked commands or let the SFTP panel follow the shell; a setting under Settings › Connection now turns it on for every connection, on by default, and each connection follows it, turns it on or turns it off; a host with another shell, no POSIX sh or an unwritable cache still gets a plain shell, and only a connection that turned it on itself is told so in a toast, so a router or a Windows server doesn't raise one on every connect; profiles, backups, sync files and restored tabs from before keep a ticked checkbox as on and read an unticked one as following the setting, so the stored choice moves to a new key that older versions ignore ([41a2d056](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/41a2d05697a27a69b1a4dfefe77d3dabab915dc6))
- let a tab or shell keep an AI agent's logo: the logos of Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and pi showed only while the agent ran, so a tab kept for one agent lost its logo between sessions; the icon picker now offers them in a group of their own, each bringing its color when picked, and a tab or shell that picks one shows it always, whichever agent runs and even with agent logos turned off, as its own choice wins over the running agent's ([3be45dd5](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/3be45dd5da422e7a56dca18a71cabb3a17746895))
- show shells' and tools' logos on tabs: bash, zsh, Git Bash and nu tabs showed generic glyphs, so they now show the Bash, Zsh, Git and Nushell logos in their brand colors, and the icon picker gains a group of 25 shell, platform, language and service logos, such as Docker, Python, Kubernetes and PostgreSQL, which bring their brand color when picked and take any color after; the logos come from Simple Icons 16.36.0 and share one drawing with the agent logos; PowerShell and Windows are missing there, fish's logo is GPL and Rust's and Neovim's are CC BY-SA, so those keep their glyphs or are left out; Bash's MIT notice and Git's CC BY 3.0 attribution join the open source licenses in the About dialog ([73a358dc](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/73a358dc6d08a71dee5960ec306c21bdbb917de8))
- show the logo of the AI agent running in a tab: while Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode or pi runs, its tab shows the agent's logo in place of the shell's or host's icon, so tabs whose titles are cut short, renamed or alike still tell which agent each holds; the agent tracker now follows which agent runs, from its first report until it ends or the prompt comes back, since an idle agent between turns is still running; an icon chosen for the tab itself still wins, and its color tints the logo; Claude Code's logo keeps its orange while the others take the text color; a switch under Tab icons turns it off, and the logos come from Simple Icons, OpenAI's from 15.22.0, the last to carry it ([c03910cb](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/c03910cbe1e5a846d8f17dc5c61e56467e39452d))
- search the settings: a field in the settings header finds settings by their title or description in the current language, each result naming its page, and the results take the page's place while the field has text; the arrow keys and Enter pick one, Esc clears the search before it closes the dialog, and opening a result goes to its page, scrolls the setting into view and briefly tints its card and colors its title; pages that are not open are not rendered, so settingsSearchIndex.ts lists each page's settings by their i18n keys, and a test checks that both languages have every key ([1d7caab4](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/1d7caab4798c45c8c429a69e496a23ab26c0e821))
- open SFTP files with a program picked for them, ask before quitting with changes not uploaded, and show large files downloading: the file menu's Open With lists the applications macOS offers for the file with their icons, or shows Windows' own Open With dialog, or asks for a program elsewhere; a quit now names the opened files whose saved changes never reached the server, alongside running tunnels; and a file over 1 MiB downloads through the transfer engine, so it shows in the transfer list with its progress and can be cancelled ([cfc35949](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/cfc3594909280e8696b3b88953677085c34de7b9))
- open SFTP files in programs on this computer: a remote file could only be edited in tTerm's own editor; the file menu now opens it in the external editor or its default program, the way WinSCP and FileZilla do. The file is downloaded to a private folder of its own, the copy is looked at once a second, and each save that differs from the server is uploaded, after asking or at once as the settings say, written in place so the file keeps its owner, mode and symlink. An upload stops to ask when the file changed on the server since it was opened, types the system would run open only in a picked program, and the drawer lists the open files with their state ([877a4b56](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/877a4b56fc7c171ebdc437357f5b300e2eef703d))
- send from the compose bar to the broadcast targets, insert saved commands into it, and suggest from history: a command for several hosts still had to go through the broadcast panel, and a saved one went straight into the terminal; with broadcast targets picked, the bar can now send to them all, at once as the panel does or line by line with a run in each connected target, the command library inserts a command into the bar on a line of its own to be looked over and sent from there, and typing a command shows the newest recent one it begins in grey, taken with Right or End ([843d3dac](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/843d3dacb1c0d0e9e3a097087e143ca88782a1c9))
- let the compose bar run several lines one at a time: pasted at once, a line that reads its input, such as a Y/n question or a password prompt, took the lines after it as answers, and a failed command did not stop the rest; with Line by line ticked, the next line now goes only once the shell is back at its prompt (OSC 133), a command that exits non-zero holds the rest until Retry, Continue or Stop, and the bar shows each line's progress, which goes on while another pane has the bar; the shell has to mark its prompts, so a shell without shell integration, or one still running a command, says so and what to turn on instead of sending ([428aaeda](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/428aaeda3755f99fa1ef744c30218a1aa947944a))
- add a compose bar that sends a whole command at once: over a slow link even with typing shown ahead, every key still went to the server; a command is now typed into a bar below the panes, where editing waits on nothing, and Enter sends it to the focused pane in one go through the terminal's own input, so it is recorded, timed and broadcast like a typed one; several lines go in as one paste where the shell takes bracketed paste, Up and Down recall recent commands, Ctrl+C with nothing selected interrupts the running command, and Esc goes back to the terminal; Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+. (iTerm2's composer key) or the terminal's context menu shows it, and a serial tab keeps its own send bar ([f2fc39b5](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/f2fc39b5962ab5494ab8e358adf91b5632d2d507))
- show typing at a remote shell before its echo comes back: over a slow link, such as a chain of jump hosts, every key waited a round trip before it showed; plain typing and backspace at the end of the shell's line are now drawn at once over the terminal, mosh style, and the server's echo confirms or takes them back, without touching the terminal's content; a line shows guesses only once the server has echoed a key typed on it, so a password prompt never shows what is typed, and full-screen programs, programs that hide the cursor and mouse-reporting programs are left alone; Settings → Connection → Typing turns it on automatically above a measured round trip of 30 ms by default (10-2000 ms, off again below two thirds of it), always, or never ([f543c04e](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/f543c04eef4b3aeaabf777add4d02b376f5c4f04))
- reuse a jump host that is already connected: a hop another connection logged in to, or a host a terminal tab is connected to, now carries the next connection that jumps through it over the same route, so a bastion is not logged in to, nor its one-time code typed, again; connections to the same hop wait for one login, as restored tabs behind one bastion do, a tab closing keeps its session for the connections still on it, and the connection test keeps its sessions to itself ([295cc78a](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/295cc78a7032b518adeb6d0ff3a28e8d878108eb))
- let a jump host log in as one of the saved connections: each hop of the chain can now be picked from the saved SSH connections instead of typed in, and keeps only the connection's id, so the hop goes where that connection points and logs in the way it does, with its saved password, even after it changes; a copy of its address stays for display and for older versions, a deleted connection says which hop to fix, and the picked connection's own jump hosts aren't followed ([d4a555db](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/d4a555db39398efbaa46247d39959ddb6613eeb0))
- list each WSL distribution as its own local shell: the new tab list, the settings and the connection dialog offered only WSL's default, so a second distribution took a custom shell to reach; the distributions are read from the registry rather than wsl -l, whose UTF-16 output and localized default marker are easy to misread, and one can be made the default shell ([0a7eba1c](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/0a7eba1c28a658dbc9421db631a0d56db6620089))
- offer a way out when a local tab's shell fails to start: a bar over the terminal shows why and lets the user edit their shell right there and start it again, try again, or open the default shell in the same directory instead of a tab with only an error in it ([9413d565](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/9413d565c91cb21638fe5663c21ec7c4d5482464))
- read quotes in a custom shell's arguments: they were split at every space, so a quoted path or command fell apart; double quotes now keep a word whole everywhere, and on macOS and Linux single quotes and backslashes work as in a POSIX shell, while on Windows a backslash stays a path separator ([9618be64](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/9618be6488adc2602c79bfe0cba163a202ff116e))
- manage local shells in Settings and pick from them wherever a local tab opens: a Local shells page lists Auto, the shells found here and the user's own, stars the default, hides found ones from the new tab list or copies one to add arguments, and adds or edits a shell with a file picker and a live check of the program it starts; the new tab list shows the default first and the user's shells after the found ones; a local terminal in the connection dialog picks from the same list or takes a program typed in, which it adds to the list or makes the default only when asked, as there was no way to set the default before; a restored tab follows its shell's later edits ([476cd991](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/476cd991d63f94967d7d20a7e70e2166443d6f76))
- keep a list of the user's own local shells in the settings, per device: a shell has a name, a program and arguments, the default can be one of them by id while its path and arguments stay in the old fields that older versions read, detected shells can be hidden from the new tab list, an older custom default becomes the first entry, a backup from another device adds only the shells found here and keeps this device's default when its own isn't, and check_local_shell tells the settings where a program path leads before a tab tries it ([7e4b78be](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/7e4b78beda5d681ed72f8a8a5bc18cbf084556de))
- let Auto start PowerShell on Windows and accept custom shell paths as users write them: Auto took %COMSPEC%, which is nearly always cmd, so PowerShell 7 and Windows PowerShell were never reached; it now tries PowerShell 7, Windows PowerShell, %COMSPEC% and cmd, in their install locations before PATH so a PATH entry on an unreachable share can't hold up a tab, and finds the shell once; a custom path may be quoted, as Explorer's Copy as path gives it, use %VARIABLES% and ~, or be a name on PATH without .exe, and one that isn't there is reported in words instead of as a spawn error ([8ed2abfe](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/8ed2abfe138fc073230fc2fb6d2e833ba83e228e))
- open every argument after -- as a directory, so tterm -- -project opens a folder whose name starts with a dash: arguments starting with - were always skipped as options ([194280f0](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/194280f0bceb0b7c2a64da462ace6c1345bcda87))
- add the tterm command when tTerm is installed on Windows, and put back what reinstalling over an older version took out: installing a new version by hand first runs the old uninstaller, which removed the command and the folder menu; Settings now keeps each choice in tTerm's local data directory, and the installer starts tTerm with --add-system-integration, which adds the command unless the user turned it off and the folder menu if they turned it on; an update brings the command to those who never turned it on, and a folder menu turned on before the choice was kept is remembered when tTerm starts ([299de6e6](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/299de6e660de36f3756b186029a829154139d7d0))
- let tterm run in tTerm's own local tabs on macOS without the command installed: the command needs a link in /usr/local/bin, which takes an administrator's password, so it cannot be added for the user; tTerm now writes the launcher at every start and adds its directory to the end of a local tab's PATH, after the user's own programs; the switch in Settings only adds or removes the link that other terminals need, and turning it off keeps the launcher the tabs use ([be041f19](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/be041f19327a623b604848bb5b4faefad2b33719))
- add Open in tTerm to the file manager's folder menu, and take tTerm's additions out on uninstall: opening a folder in tTerm meant typing its path or cd'ing to it, where Windows Terminal offers it on a right click; a second switch under System integration now adds Open in tTerm for a folder, the empty space inside one and a drive in Explorer (registry verbs under the current user, shown under Show more options on Windows 11) and, on macOS, a Finder Quick Action that runs tTerm with the chosen folders; the item is named in the app's language and follows it, and both it and the tterm command are refreshed on each start and settings save in case tTerm moved; the NSIS uninstaller now runs tTerm.exe --remove-system-integration before deleting it, unless it is updating, so no PATH entry or menu item is left pointing at a removed program ([2c1808a1](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/2c1808a16f97284fda124a061031ae5369721f7f))
- open every folder tTerm is started with, and read a drive root quoted on Windows: a file manager hands all the folders chosen in it to one command, but tTerm opened only the first; each argument that is not an option now opens a tab; and Windows reads "D:\\" as D:" because the backslash escapes the closing quote, which is how Explorer passes a drive, so a trailing quote, which no Windows path can hold, is read as the backslash it was ([9266981f](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/9266981fec1094f40314a483f993659a2f7d991e))
- add a tterm command for shells on Windows and macOS: tTerm could open a directory given on its command line, but no shell could find it by name, so `tterm .` did nothing; a switch under Settings > General > System integration now installs it: on Windows, tterm.cmd and an sh launcher for Git Bash go in a bin directory of tTerm's own (the install directory would also put uninstall and OpenConsole on the PATH), which is added to the user's PATH in the registry with a broadcast for new shells and to tTerm's own PATH for its tabs; on macOS, a launcher in tTerm's data directory is linked from /usr/local/bin, asking for an administrator's password when that directory needs one; each start points an installed launcher at the current executable, in case tTerm moved ([b77d9b3d](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/b77d9b3d786f69187b711dd1c2ed46d6b3d9e652))
- open a local terminal in the directory tTerm is started with: tTerm ignored its command line, and a second launch only raised the window, so neither `tterm .` in a shell nor a file manager's Open in tTerm could start a shell in a folder; the first argument that is not an option now names a directory, resolved against where the command ran, and opens a local tab there after the restored session (in place of the default tab when there is none), whether tTerm was starting or already running; a path that is not a folder shows a message; since an update or a relaunch starts tTerm again with the same arguments, a marker kept while such an instance runs tells the restart not to open the directory twice ([f0d087c8](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/f0d087c898c79127baa731aed1132ef9915465c2))

### Security
